verdict: Service in the window is significantly worse than the baseline on headway_sec, apt_sec, gap_share, headway_cv, service_delivered.

evidence: [A] 100% of late trains were already late at Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts (inherited delay). Origins: at or before Grant Av: 67, at Broadway Junction: 7, at Euclid Av: 5, at Utica Av: 3.
[A] 87% of headway gaps at the target already existed at Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts.

[C] 80% of late trains were already late at Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts (inherited delay). Origins: at or before Kingston-Throop Avs: 7, on approach from Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts: 3, at Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts: 2, at Lafayette Av: 1. Largest time loss on segment Lafayette Av -> Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts (median +37s vs schedule).
[C] 88% of headway gaps at the target already existed at Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts.
50% of hours with problems ran fewer than 90% of scheduled trains (overall service delivered 89%): cancellations or missing trips are creating gaps.

[C] Time is lost a little at every stop (Nostrand Av -> Franklin Av +35s, Lafayette Av -> Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts +37s, Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts -> target +29s): a dwell-time / crowding pattern rather than one bad segment.
26% of problem arrivals occurred during planned service changes (lift 2.0x).
MTA reports 'Planned ROW Work' as 26% of delays on line(s) A, C (1.1x the system share) in the analysed months.

[A] Trains that would arrive at Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts within 180s behind a C train lose 55s more there than others (p=0.000; 25% of trips affected); 26% of problem arrivals at the target had such a conflict.
MTA reports 'Infrastructure & Equipment' as 31% of delays on line(s) A, C (0.9x the system share) in the analysed months.

MTA reports 'Police & Medical' as 19% of delays on line(s) A, C (0.8x the system share) in the analysed months.

recommendations.action: Fill cancelled trips on A, C during the affected hours: check crew availability and car assignments
recommendations.rationale: Fewer trains than scheduled are running in the problem hours.
recommendations.expected_effect: Restores scheduled headways; largest APT lever available.

recommendations.action: Dwell-time programme at Jay St-MetroTech and the stops before it during the affected hours: platform controllers, door-closing announcements, step-back crews
recommendations.rationale: Run-time loss is spread across every stop on the approach, the signature of long dwells.
recommendations.expected_effect: Each stop recovers its excess dwell; the effect compounds along the line.

recommendations.action: Review merge priority and dispatch spacing at Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts, where C trains run ahead of A trains bound for Jay St-MetroTech
recommendations.rationale: Arrivals following a train of another route are disproportionately delayed.
recommendations.expected_effect: Fewer merge conflicts; smoother headways for both services.

recommendations.action: Check weekend / late-night planned service changes for A, C; use alternates F, FX
recommendations.rationale: Planned work is announced in advance.

recommendations.action: Check whether scheduled dwell and run times on the approach still match observed loads; re-time the schedule if not
recommendations.rationale: A schedule with unrealistic dwells makes every train late by design.

recommendations.action: Review the general-order (planned work) schedule for A, C; add supplement trains or move work windows off the affected hours
recommendations.rationale: Problems coincide with planned service changes.
recommendations.expected_effect: Planned changes stop degrading the analysed hours.

recommendations.action: Adjust the schedule so C and A slots are offset by at least half a headway at Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts
recommendations.expected_effect: Structural fix that survives day-to-day variability.

sources_used: NY Open Data: trains delayed / incidents
caveats: scheduled counts scaled by observed coverage (264 polling intervals); hours covered < 50% excluded from service delivered
no hour of the day worsened significantly versus the baseline; results describe the whole day
